record.title: PACMAN paper reports a real-time AI control framework deployed in DIII-D experiments
record.summary: A November 2025 author preprint, later identified in a July 2026 journal record, describes PACMAN, a real-time software framework integrating plasma diagnostics, model/controller components and actuator commands in the DIII-D tokamak control system. Its authors report five experimental applications, including reinforcement-learning control, event prediction and profile control. The manuscript gives device-specific architecture and timing details, but the deployment is CPU-based and limited to DIII-D; the paper frames extension to other devices as prospective. These are author-reported demonstrations, with no independent reproduction or matched comparative performance analysis in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that PACMAN was deployed in the DIII-D real-time plasma-control system as an end-to-end framework linking diagnostic inputs, model and controller blocks, and actuator commands. The manuscript specifies the CPU-based deployment and describes five experimental applications in §§III.1–III.5; these are author-reported experiments and have not been independently reproduced in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The manuscript reports multiple controller and prediction applications on DIII-D, including reinforcement-learning control, an ELM predictor, an Alfvén-eigenmode controller, model-predictive profile control and a tearing-mode predictor-controller. The evidence is specific to the described DIII-D shots and settings; the paper frames use on other devices as a possible extension, not demonstrated transfer.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of a PACMAN experiment, matched quantitative comparison against a predeclared baseline, or implementation on another tokamak was assessed. The manuscript reports experiments on DIII-D and states that its CPU-based design principles may be extended to other hardware and devices.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported deployment is sustained, a reusable real-time framework that connects multiple diagnostic/model/controller components to actuators across several plasma-control experiments could reduce integration barriers for AI-assisted tokamak research. The current evidence is an author-reported CPU-based deployment on DIII-D; no independent reproduction or cross-device transfer is established.
limitations: The bounded technical evidence comes from the authors' manuscript; no independent reproduction was performed.
The demonstrations concern DIII-D and CPU-based implementation. The manuscript describes extension to other hardware/devices as prospective.
The review did not quantify comparative performance, reliability against matched conventional baselines, or effects on fusion-energy output.

PPPL's direct announcement page was inaccessible during this review; the manuscript was inspected at arXiv and the July 2026 journal publication metadata was corroborated through an institutional release mirror and article record.
brief.summary: A November 2025 author preprint, later identified in a July 2026 journal record, describes PACMAN, a real-time software framework integrating plasma diagnostics, model/controller components and actuator commands in the DIII-D tokamak control system. Its authors report five experimental applications, including reinforcement-learning control, event prediction and profile control. The manuscript gives device-specific architecture and timing details, but the deployment is CPU-based and limited to DIII-D; the paper frames extension to other devices as prospective. These are author-reported demonstrations, with no independent reproduction or matched comparative performance analysis in this review.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report an integrated PACMAN deployment on DIII-D and five experimental applications in the manuscript. This is a paper-reported result, not independently reproduced here.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible author manuscript documents architecture, diagnostic/actuator interfaces, reported experiment descriptions and control-cycle details; its presence and contents are directly inspectable, while underlying experiment outcomes remain author-reported.
technical.mechanism: A modular control pipeline gathers and preprocesses diagnostic signals, applies model and controller blocks, and postprocesses actuator commands within DIII-D's real-time plasma control system.
technical.regime: DIII-D real-time plasma-control system; CPU-based implementation; the paper describes five applications with experiment-specific inputs, controllers and actuators.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper describes prior standalone ML controller demonstrations and positions PACMAN as shared integration infrastructure; this review did not compare outcomes against conventional controllers under matched settings.

brief.title: PACMAN paper reports a real-time AI control framework deployed in DIII-D experiments
brief.why_it_matters: An integrated real-time pipeline spanning diagnostics to actuator commands could lower the engineering burden of deploying different machine-learning and control approaches in fusion experiments. The evidence currently supports an author-reported CPU-based deployment and application set on one tokamak; it does not show better plasma performance than matched alternatives or transfer to a power-producing reactor.
